items.question: Which practitioner is proclaimed in Kerala as lord of sixty accomplishments?
items.inference: The verse identifies a Kerala-proclaimed practitioner grade called lord of sixty accomplishments.
uncertainties: exact ritual duties of this grade are not specified here
items.plain_english: The one proclaimed in Kerala is the lord of sixty accomplishments.

rows.grounds: compound negating meanness and related faults

items.question: What moral and qualitative marks distinguish this practitioner grade?
items.inference: The grade is marked by absence of meanness and presence of Vama-group qualities.
uncertainties: the full list of Vama-group qualities is not enumerated
items.plain_english: He is free from meanness and endowed with Vama-group qualities.

rows.grounds: compound of twenty-four accomplished ones and lordship

items.question: How is the twenty-four-accomplished lord characterized among men?

uncertainties: identity of the twenty-four accomplished ones is not detailed
items.plain_english: The lord of twenty-four accomplished ones is the best of men.

rows.grounds: compound joining upper and lower traditions

items.question: Which tradition-bearing practitioner is said to belong to great Kashmir?

items.plain_english: He who bears both upper and lower traditions is said to be of great Kashmir.

rows.grounds: compound of divine hosts and conversation

premises: gīrvāṇagaṇasaṃvādī means converse with divine hosts
items.inference: The grade is marked by converse with divine hosts and destruction of Garuda-group forces.
uncertainties: scope of Garuda-etc is not enumerated
items.plain_english: He converses with divine hosts and destroys Garuda-group forces.

rows.grounds: compound of world bliss making and hero

items.question: What heroic and devotional traits define this practitioner?
items.inference: The practitioner is a hero making world bliss, devoted to women, and conqueror of senses.
uncertainties: whether devotion to women is ritual or social is not specified
items.plain_english: He is a hero making world bliss, devoted to women, and conqueror of senses.

rows.grounds: compound of stated qualification and possession

items.question: To whom is the stated qualification said to have been mentioned before?
premises: uktādhikārasaṃpannaḥ means possessed of stated qualification
items.inference: Parvati is told that the stated qualification was mentioned before here also.
uncertainties: the exact prior passage is not identified
items.plain_english: Parvati, he is possessed of the stated qualification, as mentioned before here also.

items.question: What traits are assigned to the practitioner called Gauda?
items.inference: The practitioner called Gauda is said to have great strength and great zeal.
uncertainties: whether Gauda is regional or grade name is not clarified
items.plain_english: He of great strength and great zeal is thus called Gauda.

rows.grounds: compound of all accomplishments and giving

items.inference: The Gauda practitioner is spoken of as giver of all accomplishments.
uncertainties: conditions for receiving accomplishments are not stated
items.plain_english: Thus Gauda is spoken of as giver of all accomplishments.

items.question: What was spoken before concerning alternatives in three traditions?

uncertainties: the specific alternative is not restated in this verse
items.plain_english: In three traditions, goddess, an alternative was spoken before.

items.question: What combined conduct marks this practitioner?

uncertainties: how renunciation and enjoyment coexist is not explained
items.plain_english: He is a renouncer, enjoyer, humble, and daily tithi worshipper.

items.question: What forbidden acceptance is listed alongside another's wife and wealth?

items.plain_english: Another's wife, another's wealth, and the sixth, acceptance.
